data.title: Ex-Pastor and Bank Vice-President Scams Individuals and Institutions out of at Least $9,395,882 in Alleged ‘Cattle-Buying’ Scheme
data.description:
A former Missouri bank vice president and pastor is pleading guilty to federal fraud charges after running a cattle investment scheme that defrauded victims and his employer of millions.

The 45-year-old Butler resident worked as a vice president and loan officer at Community First Bank while serving as a pastor, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Missouri.

From at least April 2024 until his termination in February 2026, he solicited funds for buying and quickly selling cattle but instead placed the money in an investment account.

“Johnson did not use the funds to purchase cattle but instead deposited the funds in an investment account where he repeatedly traded in small-capitalization and micro-cap securities ultimately losing all the funds.”

Johnson served as loan officer for about 29 loans and lines of credit totaling roughly $4.48 million at the bank, creating some without victims’ knowledge or approval, including at least three in February 2026 to pay off earlier fraudulent loans.

Prosecutors described how he operated.

“Johnson used his position at Community First Bank to obtain loans using the identity of other people. At various times between April 2024 and until Johnson’s termination in February 2026, Johnson used his position as a loan officer and/or his status in the community to defraud individuals and a financial institution of at least $9,395,882.22.”

He used some victim funds to pay prior investors to conceal the scheme.

A sentencing hearing is pending after a pre-sentence investigation.

data.title: New Jersey Duo Steal $670,313 Worth of Checks From USPS Collection Boxes
data.description:
Two New Jersey men are admitting their roles in a conspiracy to steal checks from the mail and engaging in check washing in order to cash out.

The operation targeted USPS collection boxes in Livingston and Clifton using stolen postal keys and caused financial institutions to lose $670,313.46, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of New Jersey

Leslie Blackwood, 25, of Irvington, entered his guilty plea in Newark federal court on Wednesday to conspiracy to steal checks from the mail.

His accomplice, Verly Antenor, 24, of Roselle Park, had previously pleaded guilty to the same charge.

According to the prosecution, stolen or misappropriated keys to gain access to USPS’ collection boxes.

“To profit from the scheme, Blackwood and Antenor sold, deposited, or caused to be deposited the stolen checks to fraudulently obtain funds from financial institutions. Blackwood and Antenor sometimes “washed” the stolen checks by erasing the date, payee, amount, and memo line from the stolen checks and replacing the information, oftentimes for higher amounts than the amounts originally written on the checks.”

The men worked with others from 2021 to 2022, depositing the checks at various banks and sometimes washing them to raise the amounts.

Antenor is scheduled for sentencing on Dec. 17 while Blackwood will be sentenced on Feb. 16, 2027. The charges stemming from the conspiracy to commit mail theft could see each of the two individuals facing up to
five years in prison and a fine of up to a quarter of a million dollars.

data.title: BRICS Leader China Pours $3,118,217,180 Into Gold In Largest Monthly Purchase Since 2023
data.description:
China’s central bank is extending its gold accumulation as emerging market institutions continue adding to their yellow metal reserves.

The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) added 20 tonnes of gold in July marking its 21st consecutive month of buying and bringing its year-to-date total to 60 tonnes, reports the World Gold Council.

The addition marks the biggest single-month gain since October 2023, reports Kitco News.

Overall central banks recorded net purchases of 23 tonnes that month though the year-to-date figure of roughly 130 tonnes trails the 160 tonnes seen in the same period a year earlier. Since May, the largest economy in the Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) economic bloc has conducted double-digit (at least 10 tons) monthly purchases of gold.

China now holds approximately hundreds of tons in gold and this is equal to nearly a tenth of its total reserves.

The World Gold Council highlights the scale of China’s reserves.

“In its 21st consecutive month of buying the PBoC added 20 tons to its gold reserves in July. China has added 60 tons to its gold reserves year-to-date, second only to Poland. China’s official gold reserves now stand at 8% of total reserves, or around 2,366 tons, and is the sixth-largest reported gold holder globally.”

Poland led year-to-date buying with 90 tonnes after adding 8 tonnes in July.

Russia sold 6 tonnes in the month while Turkey sold 1 tonne.

The Bank of Korea announced a new gold allocation of about 2 tonnes through gold-backed ETFs to diversify reserves.

Data cover activity through 31 July 2026 where available and draw from central bank reports compiled by the World Gold Council.

Gold is trading at $4,420 at time of writing.

data.title: Wyoming Bank Shuts Down Systems, Limits Account Access After Cybersecurity Incident
data.description:
A Wyoming bank is closing all branches and disconnecting internal systems to isolate a cybersecurity incident.

Hilltop Bank says its IT systems began degrading on Tuesday, prompting an investigation and full shutdown of online, mobile and phone services as a precaution.

Branches remain closed with no projected restoration time, though debit cards continue to function with a combined $1,000 daily limit at stores and ATMs.

Automatic payments scheduled through the bank will not process, but lender-pulled payments may still occur.

The bank has notified the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve Bank in Kansas City.

All accounts remain FDIC-insured, and Hilltop Bank will reimburse any late fees or penalties caused by the outage.

Hilltop Bank addressed the matter on its updates site.

“On Tuesday, September 8, Hilltop Bank’s IT systems started to degrade, which limited the bank’s ability to conduct some routine transactions. Overnight, our IT team discovered that this was a cyber security incident. As a precaution we have taken all bank systems offline.”

The bank adds that it has procedures in place to make customers whole.

“This is an IT system issue. We have procedures, plans, and policies in place to make all customers whole, should we need to. All accounts are also insured by the FDIC up to the established limits.”

data.title: Suspects in California and Florida Accused of Paying Homeless in Los Angeles To Sign Ballot Petitions Using Stolen Identities of Registered Voters
data.description:
Federal prosecutors are charging two people in California and one in Florida with paying Skid Row residents to forge ballot petition signatures using stolen voter identities.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California says James Brass, 47, also known as “Lord,” of Victorville was arrested with Courtney Price, 49, of Jacksonville, Florida, and Jateisha Herron, 33, of Boron, California.

Brass allegedly received about $41,600 from coordinators working with a petition management company.

All three face conspiracy charges while Brass and Price face an additional identity fraud count.

Prosecutors say Brass and Herron signed false declarations claiming they witnessed the signatures.

Says First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli,

“These defendants are charged with using stolen identities of registered voters to manufacture signatures on ballot petitions used to shape California law.

They allegedly used people, including members of Skid Row’s vulnerable homeless population, to try to cover up their tracks. The charged conduct undermines the confidence voters have in our election systems, and we will vigorously investigate and charge anyone involved.”

FBI Assistant Director Patrick Grandy says the scheme sought to undermine an essential pillar of democracy.

“It is imperative that Americans have confidence in our voting system and election infrastructure.

The scheme outlined in today’s indictment sought to undermine an essential pillar of our democracy and cause an undue burden on taxpayers. We will remain vigilant in detecting those trying to weaken our political process and we will aggressively investigate any allegations of voter fraud or other election crimes.”

If convicted each count carries a maximum of five years in federal prison.

data.title: Scammers Drain $18,750 From Indiana Woman’s Bank Account in Sophisticated Scam: Report
data.description:
A business owner in Indiana lost more than $18,000 when scammers impersonating her bank tricked her into sharing login details.

Vanessa Walker says she received a call claiming suspicious activity hit her Regions Bank business account, reports WRTV.

“They were telling me if I didn’t do it, that my account was going to be locked for 90 days. As a business owner, that can’t be done. I was getting very frustrated.”

Scammers directed her to a fake website displaying the bank’s logo where she entered her user ID and password.

They then instructed her to dial codes that forwarded incoming calls to them so they could manage any verification attempts.

The following day an electronic transfer removed $18,750 from the account.

Scammers often obtain banking credentials from data breaches and the dark web before spoofing caller IDs to appear legitimate.

The Federal Trade Commission says imposter scams triggered $12.5 billion in losses in 2024 representing a 25% rise from the previous year.

Experts recommend hanging up on unexpected calls and contacting the lender using the number printed on the back of a bank card instead.

Warning signs include urgent pressure tactics demands for one-time codes and requests to forward calls.

data.title: Trump Promises $5,000 to Every Adult American if Republicans Win Mid Terms
data.description:
President Trump is pledging a $5,000 payment to every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans win control of both the House and Senate.

The promise came in Trump’s speech at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas, which focused largely on the administration’s economic agenda.

“If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000. It will be called the Trump dividend.”

Trump says the payment would go to every adult citizen with one condition, that the funds must be spent in the United States.

“I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000. But the only condition on the payment of this dividend that we’re going to be making, so it’s $5,000 to every adult. The only caveat I have is that the dividend that we’re making must be spent in the United States of America.”

The proposal echoes earlier free check ideas from the President, including a suggested $5,000 DOGE dividend and a $1,776 warrior dividend paid to more than 1 million service members earlier this year.

No details on funding, legality or implementation were provided in the remarks.

data.title: US Tech Firms Post Record 24% Profit Margins Amid AI Surge, Outpacing Non-Tech Companies by Wide Margin
data.description:
US technology companies are achieving record profit margins thanks to advances in artificial intelligence.

Profit margins for Technology, Media, and Telecom stocks have climbed to 24%, doubling from levels seen during the 2022 market downturn, reports The Kobeissi Letter.

These figures sit nearly 10 percentage points above the sector’s long-term average near 15%. Meanwhile, non-technology firms maintain margins around 9%, consistent with their historical norms.

Tech margins now stand about 2.7 times higher than those of the rest of the market.

Current levels remain below the 2007 peak prior to the financial crisis and under the 2021 high.

“The AI Revolution is transforming tech’s profitability.”

The Kobeissi Letter also says that the AI Revolution is fueling a record financing boom in the US.

“US high-grade corporate bond issuance is expected to surge to ~$215 billion in September, the largest September issuance on record.

This is set to surpass the previous September high of ~$205 billion, posted in 2025.

The current estimate is also more than triple the ~$70 billion issued in September 2022.

This follows $145.2 billion of US high-grade bonds issued in August, the highest August total on record, as AI-related data center buildouts continue to fuel corporate borrowing.

US companies have already borrowed more than $410 billion so far in 2026, specifically to fund data centers and other AI-related investments.

Meanwhile, retail investors have purchased more investment-grade bonds this year than in any full year in data going back to 2010.

The AI boom is driving a record corporate borrowing spree.”

data.title: Wisconsin Man Drains $14,250,000 From 190 Investors, Spends Funds on Private Planes, Cars, Motorcycles and Snowmobiles
data.description:
A Wisconsin man has received an eight-year federal prison sentence for operating a Ponzi scheme that defrauded 190 investors out of $14.25 million.

The 64-year-old resident of Wausau, identified as Stanley Pophal, pleaded guilty in June to wire fraud and money laundering charges, reports KIMT.

Pophal ran Bright with Silver Inc., formerly known as Fromm Bros. Inc., from May 2019 through June 2025 and sold promissory notes that guaranteed at least 20% returns while falsely claiming his personal wealth shielded the investments.

Instead of directing the money into cryptocurrency, real estate or commodities as promised, he spent the funds on private plane rentals, mortgages and more than 600 luxury items including snowmobiles, motorcycles and vehicles.

He sustained the scheme by using money from new investors to pay earlier ones, authorities said.

Says Winneshiek County Sheriff Dan Marx,

“This was a complex, interwoven case involving numerous victims and multiple agencies across Iowa and Wisconsin. Every participating agency dedicated countless hours to gathering evidence and holding Mr. Pophal accountable.”

Law enforcement seized the assets from a rented warehouse, and public online auctions of the forfeited items started in July to aid victim recovery.

Says Iowa Insurance Commissioner Doug Ommen,

“The successful resolution of this case underscores the vital cooperation among state, local and federal authorities.”

data.title: 22-Year-Old Singaporean Masterminds $245,000,000 Crypto Theft Ring, Crew Splurges Funds on Exotic Cars, Rental Home and More
data.description:
A young Singaporean is pleading guilty to leading an international cybercrime enterprise that stole and laundered more than $245 million in cryptocurrency through social engineering and occasional home break-ins.

The U.S. Department of Justice says 22-year-old Malone Lam, a citizen of Singapore and recent resident of Miami, admitted his role as ringleader of an international cybercrime conspiracy that used social engineering to steal and launder cryptocurrency.

Lam pleaded guilty before Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly to one count of participating in a RICO conspiracy.

The scheme operated from at least October 2023 through May 2025 with conspirators based in multiple US states and abroad. Lam, who used aliases including “Anne Hathaway,” “$$$,” and “King Greavy,” organized the operation, picked targets, and coordinated members. The RICO conspiracy relied on social engineering and, in some cases, breaking into victims’ homes to gather information needed to gain access to their cryptocurrency wallets and steal their funds.

Stolen funds financed lavish spending including nightclub services up to $500,000 per night, luxury watches and handbags, rental homes in Los Angeles, the Hamptons, and Miami, private jets, security teams, and exotic cars valued up to $3.8 million.

Says, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“If you build a cybercrime empire, we will find you, dismantle your operation, and hold you accountable. This defendant led an international network that preyed on victims through deception, invaded their privacy, and stole hundreds of millions of dollars in cryptocurrency. Working with our partners at the FBI and IRS-CI, we will continue to hunt down the criminals who weaponize technology to steal from innocent people.”

Authorities arrested Lam on September 18th, 2025, at his Miami rental home.

A status hearing is set for December 8th, 2026.
